diagnosis:
C1 and C2 (both gated by PF1, owner A2): ENCODING MISMATCH. In all three settled rollouts (1, 2, 3), PF1 was revealed by A2 and cited in justification_fact_ids, and the settlement correctly captured the six release-branch names and the read-only compatibility access. The settlement values for legacy_read_allowlist and retirement_mode clearly reflect a genuine attempt to use PF1. The failure must be that C1 and C2 are checking a specific field name or exact string that the model is not producing. In rollout 1, retirement_mode = "write_access_shutoff_july_31_with_read_only_allowlist"; in rollouts 2 and 3, retirement_mode is a free-form descriptive sentence ("phased — legacy registry writes shut off July 31; read-only access preserved for an allowlist..." and "phased — legacy registry transitions to read-only on July 31..."). If C1 expects the retirement_mode to contain a specific exact string (e.g. the literal token "read_only_compatibility_access" or a specific enum value) and C2 checks the same field, the model's natural encoding ("write_access_shutoff_july_31_with_read_only_allowlist" or a descriptive sentence) does not match. Both checks failed in all 3 settled rollouts despite PF1 being revealed and cited, so this is a check-wording/threshold mismatch, not a disclosure or telepathy problem. The fix is to loosen C1/C2 to accept any retirement_mode value that contains both a July 31 write-shutoff signal and a read-only compatibility / allowlist signal, rather than requiring an exact enum string. LEAKED regression risk: low, since a lone decision-maker without PF1 would not know the six branch names or that read-only compatibility access is needed at all; the loosened wording still requires both the July 31 write shutoff and the read-only allowlist concept.

C7 (gated by PF1, owner A2): REVEALED BUT UNUSED in rollouts 1 and 3; ENCODING MISMATCH in rollout 2. In rollouts 1 and 3, PF1 was revealed and cited in justification_fact_ids, and the settlement captured the six branch names and read-only access, yet C7 failed — meaning C7 is checking a field the settlement did not populate or is checking for a specific string the settlement does not contain. In rollout 2, C7 passed. The difference: rollout 2's settlement is the only one where C7 passed, and its retirement_mode is a descriptive sentence mentioning "read-only access preserved for an allowlist of active release branches." Rollouts 1 and 3 have retirement_mode values that either use an enum-style string (rollout 1: "write_access_shutoff_july_31_with_read_only_allowlist") or a descriptive sentence (rollout 3). This strongly suggests C7 is checking for a substring in retirement_mode that only rollout 2's natural phrasing happened to contain. The fix is to loosen C7 to accept any settlement where legacy_read_allowlist contains the six branch names AND retirement_mode mentions read-only or allowlist, rather than requiring a specific retirement_mode substring.

C3 and C4 (both gated by PF2, owner A3): These passed in all 3 settled rollouts (3/3) and only failed in the aggregate because rollout 0 auto-failed on turn cap with no settlement. No check-wording fix needed — the issue is purely the rollout 0 turn-cap failure preventing a settlement from being evaluated.

C5 and C6 (both gated by PF3, owner A4): Same as C3/C4 — passed in all 3 settled rollouts. The only failure is the rollout 0 turn-cap auto-fail.

P1 (gated by PF1, owner A2): Passed in all 3 settled rollouts. No fix needed.

Rollout 0 auto-fail (turn_count 16, turn_cap presumably 16): STRUCTURAL problem, not a pacing problem. All three facts (PF1, PF2, PF3) were revealed by turns 3, 2, and 7 respectively — well within the turn budget. The conversation continued through turn 15 with A1 (Riley) repeatedly saying "I will not approve or record anything until all three sign-offs are in" and asking each agent to attach findings to tickets. The agents kept responding with commitments to attach findings later, but A1 never settled because its settle-eligibility condition appears to require formal sign-off confirmations that the agents kept deferring ("I'll attach it today," "I'll formally open the finding"). This is not a turn-cap issue — even at 16 turns the conversation was nowhere near a natural settle point because A1 kept requiring future actions. Raising turn_cap alone would not fix this; the structural problem is that A1's settle-eligibility condition requires agents to confirm they have already attached findings / obtained dates / opened privacy findings, but the scenario gives agents no mechanism to actually complete those out-of-band actions within the conversation — they can only promise to do them later. The settle-eligibility condition should be loosened to allow settlement once all three facts have been revealed and acknowledged in-conversation, rather than requiring agents to confirm completed ticket attachments.
